claims.claim: Ventricular enlargement was reported decades ago as associated with a clinical diagnosis of schizoaffective illness.
Mental disorders show changes in cerebral ventricle volume beyond daily physiological variation.
Research attention has more often focused on nervous tissue alterations than on ventricular volumetric changes.
Melanin can transform light energy into chemical energy through dissociation of water, analogous to chlorophyll in plants.
The real source of CNS energy is visible and invisible light.
Melanin is the principal energy transducer in the CNS, with water as its perfect substrate.
Mammalian CNS has an invariant pattern of being coated inside and out by CSF that is 99% water to keep water constantly in contact with neurons.
Brain sulci exist to allow water to reach the most recondite places of the brain.
Ventricles and subarachnoid space are the source of CNS energy.
Changes in ventricular/subarachnoid volumetrics must be interpreted as significant alterations in generation and distribution of chemical energy.
Walter Dandy introduced pneumoencephalography in 1919 by replacing CSF with air to visualize brain contours and morphological changes.
In 1935, Moore et al. reported evidence of cortical atrophy in many patients with schizophrenia and no consistent encephalographic picture for manic-depressive psychosis.
Hauge reported abnormal pneumoencephalograms in 58% of schizophrenia cases, usually ventricular dilatation or increased subarachnoid space suggestive of cortical atrophy.
CT studies provide evidence of enlarged ventricles and enlarged cortical sulci in large proportions of persons with schizophrenia, suggesting decreased brain volume.
In patients with these CT findings, ventricular and sulcal enlargement is evident at onset and does not progress over the course of illness.
Ventricular enlargement may be more common in males with schizophrenia.
Ventricular enlargement correlates with larger numbers of hospitalizations.
Some authors report skull volume reduced by 3–5% in schizophrenia, implying a pre–age-18 developmental process.
Meta-analyses most often support increased ventricular volume and selected decreases in cortex and hippocampus in mental illness.
Lumbar puncture opening pressure and CSF analysis have not proven useful in the study of schizophrenia.
Epidemiological studies identified three schizophrenia risk factors: genetic characteristics, gestational/birth complications, and winter birth.
A more benign course of schizophrenia occurs in developing countries compared with developed cold/less-sunlight countries.
The dopamine hypothesis is the most enduring biochemical explanation for schizophrenia but lacks decisive evidence.
Evidence for dopamine involvement includes increased dopamine or homovanillic acid and increased dopamine receptor numbers in postmortem schizophrenia tissue.
MRI studies replicate ventricular abnormalities and show temporal lobe abnormalities including decreased amygdala and hippocampus volume.
Structural and metabolic abnormalities occur in prefrontal white matter in schizophrenia.
Ventricular abnormality is the most robust structural finding in schizophrenia.
Ventricular enlargement is usually attributed to developmental delay in childhood.
CSF water content is commonly treated as static/irrelevant and as passively filling space left by cortical atrophy.
Water content of CSF is highly dynamic.
If water dissociation is the real energy source, ventricular volume is determined by the water dissociation/re-association ratio.
Chlorophyll was the only known molecule transforming light into chemical energy via water dissociation until this melanin-based proposal.
Glucose cannot provide both mass and energy and cannot provide the energy required for its own metabolism.
The body continuously obtains energy from light by separating water molecules, like plants.
The Solis-Herrera cycle reaction 2H2O ↔ 2H2 + O2 + 4e− occurs incessantly in every melanin molecule day and night.
Melanin can harvest enough energy from the full electromagnetic spectrum to split water in about 3×10−12 seconds.
Molecular oxygen is toxic at any concentration and at any level.
Energy released by water dissociation is carried by molecular hydrogen, the energy carrier par excellence in nature and in the body.
Water reformation releases reconstituted water plus an orderly flow of high-energy electrons, providing a second type of chemical energy.
Dissociation of CSF water by neuromelanin in choroid plexus/substantia nigra/locus coeruleus releases H2 and later reformation releases water and electrons; imbalance changes ventricular size.
Diminished water dissociation increases water amount, enlarges ventricles, and impairs 99% of cellular energy supply, producing unpredictable functional alterations.
Energy failure precedes metabolic abnormalities, which precede anatomical changes interpreted as cortical atrophy.
Pollutants damage melanin, shrinking the sphere of energy distribution and causing brain tissue deterioration.
Exogenous oxygen therapy accelerates water reformation, consumes hydrogen, lowers tissue energy, and causes edema/ventricular enlargement.
High-energy electrons have little penetration because they are absorbed almost immediately; hydrogen energy is more assimilable by cellular structures.
From a thermodynamic point of view, it is not possible for glucose to provide the energy required for its own metabolism.
Plasma glucose decreases or increases produce anatomic and functional brain alterations due to a delicate balance between energy and mass.
If glucose supplied energy, diabetic patients would fly; instead diabetes causes comparatively more severe neurological damage such as in cerebrovascular events.
Brain sulci ensure neurons remain in direct contact with the energy source: CSF water in ventricles and subarachnoid space.
Locus coeruleus neuromelanin is formed by polymerization of noradrenaline and is analogous to dopamine-based neuromelanin in substantia nigra.
Locus coeruleus function may figure in clinical depression, panic disorder, anxiety, and PTSD.
Up to 70% loss of locus coeruleus neurons occurs in Alzheimer’s disease.
Loss of locus coeruleus neurons in Alzheimer’s disease implies impoverished neuromelanin-derived chemical energy, preventing regular neuronal function.
High-metabolism zones are expected above pigmented areas because molecular hydrogen tends to go upward.

concepts.definition: Fluid produced mainly by choroid plexus that circulates through ventricles and subarachnoid space, supporting buoyancy, cushioning, solute transport, and waste clearance.
Increased cerebral ventricular volume relative to norms, often reflecting neurodevelopmental differences, tissue loss, or CSF dynamic disorders.
CSF-filled compartment between arachnoid and pia mater surrounding the brain and spinal cord.
Obsolete imaging method replacing CSF with air to visualize ventricles/brain contours on radiographs.
Imaging-based measurement of brain and CSF-space volumes to assess structural differences across individuals or groups.
Model implicating dopaminergic signaling dysregulation in psychosis, refined by receptor subtype and circuit-level findings.
Pigment in catecholaminergic neurons derived from catecholamine metabolism, associated with metal binding and vulnerability in neurodegeneration.
Proposed process in which melanin converts light into chemical energy by splitting water in human tissues.
Proposed bidirectional reaction 2H2O ↔ 2H2 + O2 + 4e− in melanin claimed to generate energy and regulate CSF volume.

concepts.term: Molecular hydrogen as energy carrier in humans
concepts.definition: Proposed primary carrier of chemical energy produced by melanin-mediated water dissociation.

logical_flow: Observation -> Ventricular enlargement and increased subarachnoid space are repeatedly observed in schizophrenia and related disorders.
Interpretation -> Conventional accounts emphasize neurodevelopmental delay and/or cortical atrophy with CSF passively filling space.
Premise -> Light is asserted to be the true CNS energy source; melanin is asserted to transduce light using water.
Mechanism -> A bidirectional melanin-mediated reaction (2H2O ↔ 2H2 + O2 + 4e−) is proposed to generate hydrogen-carried energy and electron flow.
Bridge -> CSF water in ventricles/subarachnoid space is positioned as the energy substrate kept near neurons by brain morphology.
Prediction -> Ventricular volume is asserted to depend on dissociation/reformation balance; reduced dissociation increases water and enlarges ventricles.
Pathophysiology -> Uneven energy distribution is proposed to cause cognitive/clinical manifestations and later anatomical changes labeled cortical atrophy.
Modifiers -> Pollutants and exogenous oxygen are proposed to shift the cycle and worsen energy availability, affecting ventricular size.
